label: Experiments A and B (faculty plan of 2026-11-13, AUDIT.md section 16): the four scenarios, the two small maps and the run settings of the SIMULATOR study (hri_sim_v4.scenario_ab, run_experiments_ab_v4.py). Simulator only: nothing here is a measurement.
declared: 2026-11-13, before any code (AUDIT.md section 16.2 and 16.4). Maps and placements are Anisha's decisions of 2026-11-13; the numbers marked CHOSEN were chosen by the AI where neither the plan nor the answers settle them, listed in AUDIT.md 16.4 for Anisha to confirm.

avoid_people.why: Decided 2026-11-13 (Anisha, AUDIT.md 16.5): the simulator's routes are straight lines, so with a second person to ask the robot bumped or stalled at the other avatar even with truthful workers (A3 detection on: 5 of 20 collisions). When enabled the simulator adds a detour waypoint around any person a route passes closer than clearance = the safety corridor half-width of hri_control.json (0.6 m) + half the robot width of robot.json (0.3 m) = 0.9 m, as Unity's NavMesh agent would. No new tuned number; the 1.25 factor of the waypoint offset is geometry (both legs clear the person), not a setting.

placement_rule.why: Decided 2026-11-13 (Anisha, AUDIT.md 16.11), after the first runs: any two workers at least 3.0 m apart, and every worker at least 3.0 m from every turning point of the path (the start node and every junction), so that asking one worker cannot leave the robot (2.0 m from them) inside the person-in-path stop zone (0.85 m at standstill) of another: 3.0 - 2.0 = 1.0 m > 0.85 m. The v3 person-in-path stop is unchanged. Applies to the layouts 'beside' (checked, 4.0 m apart and 3.6 m from the node) and 'random' (enforced by the sampling; replaces its earlier min_sep_m 1.0). UNITY MUST USE THE SAME RULE when it places the workers of these experiments (for Nusrat): at least 3.0 m between any two workers and at least 3.0 m from every junction and from the start node.

B.note: each worker is a liar with this probability, drawn ONCE per worker per run (lie_mode per_worker, AUDIT.md 16.12 item 2, as Unity: a liar shows the same wrong direction every time it is asked in that run); lie_mode per_gesture is the earlier model of 16.2 decision 2 (every gesture an independent draw)

corridor.label: A1: one straight road A to B, no branch. CHOSEN: 40 m north (the length of the route A to E1 of the v4 map).

turn.label: A2: A to B to C, one 90-degree right turn at B, no other branch. CHOSEN: 20 m north, then 20 m east.

turn_left.label: A2 with a LEFT turn: the mirror of turn, taken unchanged from Nusrat's proposal Scenario/Config/roadmap_proposals/turn_left.json (2026-11-14): 20 m north, then 20 m west; C (-13.75, 0).

1.title: straight corridor A to B, 2 avatars, one on each side

2.title: A to B to C with a right-angle turn at B, 2 avatars at each asking node (A and B), one on each side

3.title: A to a random goal on the v4 map, people beside the road at every asking node (A and J1 to J4)

4.title: A to a random goal on the v4 map, people at random places around every asking node

why.layout.beside: Decision 3 of 2026-11-13: one person on each side of the arriving road, lateral_m 2.0 from its centre line, before_m 3.0 before the node along the arrival direction (at the start node A: 3.0 m behind A, along the opposite of the start heading).
why.layout.random: Decision 3 of 2026-11-13: a 6 m x 6 m square (half_size_m 3.0) centred on the node, at least min_road_m 1.0 from every road centre line; the separation of the workers and their distance from the turning points come from placement_rule (3.0 m each, decision of the third round); rejection sampling seeded by run and node.
why.goal: random_endpoint = one of the endpoints of the map, uniformly, from random.Random(f"{seed}|goal") over the sorted endpoint names.
why.trial_timeout_s: CHOSEN: the v4 value of final_plan.json (270 s). A run that backtracks and runs out of time is a FAILURE (timeout) and is reported as such.
why.first_seed: CHOSEN: run k of a scenario uses seed first_seed + k - 1 (1 to 20). Simulator seeds only; no final run is involved.
why.gesture simulation: The neutral defaults of hri_sim_v4.GestureSimConfig (coverage 1, accuracy 1, no angle noise) and SimConfig (no 360 noise): the lie is the only error source; the mirror ambiguity of the pointing arm and the second view stay as they are.
why.layout.people_by_node: Decided 2026-11-14 (Anisha, AUDIT.md 16.12 item 3): a third worker at J1 in A3, A4, B3, B4 so that the majority vote of rule (a) has three voters; the other nodes keep 2. In 'beside' the third worker stands 3.0 m behind the first, on its side.
why.layout.nearer_margin_m: Decided 2026-11-14 (Anisha, AUDIT.md 16.12 item 4), as Nusrat's random layout in Unity: every worker after the first is at least 0.25 m farther from the robot than the first at every point of the last approach_m 3.0 m of the arrival road (at the start node: from the start position), so the first worker is the one the robot reaches first; the 3.0 m spacing rule of placement_rule is unchanged. max_draws 100000 as in Unity.
why.alternative_maps: turn_left (Nusrat's proposal, adopted as a map of the experiments 2026-11-14) is the left-turn A2; the default is the right turn of 16.2 decision 1; run_scenario(..., side='left') uses it.

detection.why: Review of 2026-11-13 (Anisha, AUDIT.md 16.10): 'on' of the experiments is second opinion + reject impossible. Backtrack (rule c) is kept as a switch in control.json but is OFF in the experiments: in 80 detection-on runs it was never used and in the 80 reject + backtrack runs it fired once and that run ended in the wrong goal. hri_sim_v4.DETECTION_OFF / DETECTION_ON equal these two blocks (a test pins it).
